profile.reading:
This building sits in the Highway 370 Industrial Park in Sarpy County, part of the broader area around Google's original Nebraska data center campus in Papillion, which broke ground on 275 acres in late 2019 at a reported cost of roughly $600 million, Google's first Nebraska facility. Google has continued to expand the Papillion site and surrounding Sarpy County parcels in the years since, and a company spokesperson has described staff progression from Papillion into leadership roles at Google's newer Lincoln, Nebraska campus, illustrating how the original site anchored Google's broader Nebraska workforce. Since 2019, Google has created more than 120 jobs across computer technician, engineer, maintenance, and food service roles at its Nebraska sites, which the company has said it declines to break out by individual location. Google reports investing about $4.4 billion in Nebraska cumulatively over the five years through 2024, including $930 million in 2024 alone, spread across the Papillion, northwest Omaha, and Lincoln campuses. Google's own Nebraska data center location page does not identify which specific building in the Highway 370 Industrial Park this OSM-mapped structure corresponds to, nor its individual square footage or MW capacity, so this registry records the $4.4 billion statewide figure as regional context rather than a fact specific to this building, and flags a Sarpy County Assessor parcel lookup as the next real research step.

Omaha Public Power District, which serves the Douglas and Sarpy county campuses, has cited large-load data center demand from Google and other operators as a leading factor in its own long-range generation and transmission planning, and Nebraska's status as one of the few states where electricity is delivered entirely by public power districts rather than investor-owned utilities has repeatedly come up in coverage of why Google, Facebook, and other hyperscalers chose the Omaha-Lincoln corridor for a dense cluster of campuses.

reading.body:
Google broke ground on this Sarpy County campus in late 2019 on 275 acres at a reported cost of roughly $600 million, and has continued to expand the site and surrounding parcels since. Google does not publish capacity in megawatts at the building level in this industrial park, so the scale of this facility cannot be determined from operator specs. The company has invested approximately $4.4 billion across Nebraska over five years through 2024, including $930 million in 2024 alone, spread across the Papillion, northwest Omaha, and Lincoln campuses, and has created more than 120 jobs in computer technician, engineer, maintenance, and food service roles across its Nebraska sites.

Nebraska's electricity is delivered entirely by public power districts rather than investor-owned utilities, a fact that has repeatedly been cited in coverage of why Google and other hyperscalers chose the Omaha-Lincoln corridor for a dense cluster of campuses. Omaha Public Power District, which serves the Sarpy County site, has identified large-load data center demand from Google and other operators as a leading factor in its own long-range generation and transmission planning.

No individual building capacity is published for this facility, and 21 mapped facilities in Nebraska have no published megawatt figures. This campus matters to AI compute scaling to the degree that Nebraska's open public power infrastructure and Google's demonstrated commitment to the state anchor the hyperscaler cluster in the Omaha-Lincoln corridor, but individual site capacity remains opaque without a Sarpy County Assessor parcel lookup.
